name: Bandırma
title: Bandırma Ship Thickness Gauging | Fertiliser & Boron Ships
description: Thickness gauging at Bandırma for bulk carriers, fertiliser and boron cargoes, ro-ro and general cargo ships: UTM of holds, tanks and decks during port calls.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for Ships at Bandırma, Southern Marmara
intro: Bandırma is the main port of Turkey's southern Marmara coast, sheltered at the head of its own bay and serving the industrial towns of Balıkesir province. Bulk carriers load and discharge boron products, fertiliser materials and grain, ro-ro and ferry traffic links the port with Istanbul, and general cargo ships work the quays. Cargoes like these are hard on hold steel, which is why gauging is asked for here. Technicians travel from India to the ship at the berth or the bay anchorage.
keywords: bulk carrier hold frame gauging turkey

highlights.p: Chemical powders and fertiliser raw materials are abrasive and corrosive. Bulk carriers that load or discharge them here show wear on tank tops, lower hold frames and coatings, and gauging after discharge shows how much.

Handysize and Supramax ships bring grain and bulk materials to the quays. Hold work is possible once cargo is out and the crew has cleaned, with the port's cargo plans deciding the length of the window.
Ro-ro vessels and ferries serve the port on regular routes. Ramps, car decks and ballast tanks can be gauged during scheduled layovers, with access agreed around vehicle loading.

p: Bandırma lies in a bay on the southern shore of the Sea of Marmara, in Balıkesir province, sheltered from the open sea by the Kapıdağ peninsula and the coast around Erdek. The harbour is protected and approached by a pilotage route, and ships at the anchorage in the bay are in calmer water than the exposed northern Marmara coast. The town is connected to Istanbul by sea, by road and by a long-standing rail line, so cargo and passengers use the port in both directions.

The cargo mix leans towards industrial materials. Boron products from nearby mines and processing plants are among the best-known exports, and fertiliser raw materials arrive for the chemical works close to the port. Grain, cement, steel and general cargo pass through the same quays, and the port also handles ro-ro traffic and ferry services. Bulk carriers in the Handysize and Supramax range predominate, with general cargo ships and coasters carrying the regional trade and ro-ro vessels moving trailers and vehicles.

That traffic leaves marks on steel. Boron compounds and fertiliser materials are dusty, can be damp, and attack coatings, while repeated grab discharge scrapes tank tops and lower hold frames. An owner running a ship in these trades may find that the hold structure ages faster than the hull outside, and surveyors will ask for readings before accepting coatings as fit. Because ships here usually discharge and reload at a pace set by the shipper, the gauging window is the time the holds are clean, empty and certified, which can be shorter than a superintendent would wish.

At the commercial quays, work is done alongside after discharge. Holds are measured once the crew has swept and washed them and the area has been certified for entry, concentrating on tank tops, lower hold frames and brackets, hopper plating, hatch coamings and the plating beneath the grab-working zone. On general cargo ships and coasters the sequence is similar, with extra attention to tween-deck structure. The terminal's permit and access system governs entry, and the agent supplies passes in advance. Work is planned around the loading programme so the holds go back to the ship on time.

Ro-ro ships and ferries can be gauged during scheduled layovers on their berths, covering ramps, car decks and ballast tanks, though the windows are shorter. At the bay anchorage the agent can arrange launches for ships waiting for berths, which suits deck, hatch cover and ballast tank readings. The port does not offer a drydock for large ships, so those needing a dry hull normally go to Tuzla, to the Yalova yards or to a yard elsewhere on the Marmara, with Bandırma readings sent ahead to shape the steel estimate.
list: Commercial quays — hold frames, tank tops, hopper plating and coamings on bulk carriers and general cargo ships after discharge
Boron and fertiliser berths — hold and deck gauging on ships working abrasive and corrosive cargoes, with coating condition noted
Ro-ro and ferry berths — ramps, car decks and ballast tanks gauged during scheduled layovers
Bay anchorage — deck, hatch cover and ballast tank gauging on ships awaiting a berth, reached by launch
General cargo and coaster berths — tween-deck and hold structure on regional trade ships
Docking elsewhere on the Marmara — readings carried to a yard's steel estimate

context.h: Port state control and industrial trade context
p: Ships calling at Bandırma are inspected under the Black Sea MoU and Mediterranean MoU regimes Turkey participates in, with the harbour master's office and the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure acting for the state. Bulk carriers and general cargo ships in the industrial trades attract attention for hold condition and hatch covers, and structural findings can lead the inspecting officer to ask for gauging records. Class societies, including Türk Loydu alongside the larger international ones, expect measured thickness for plates the surveyor considers suspect during renewal surveys.

Commercially, the port's cargoes come from agriculture and chemical industry rather than from containers, and the owners who work them range from Turkish bulk fleets to small regional operators. Boron and fertiliser charterers sometimes want evidence that holds are in sound condition before loading, and sale and purchase deals in Handysize tonnage are common, so pre-purchase gauging has a regular place here. Ships that go on to EU ports must also carry a current Inventory of Hazardous Materials and report under the EU's carbon rules for those voyages.

psc: Black Sea MoU and Mediterranean MoU

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Bandırma
jobs.p: Bandırma work is driven by cargo type. After a boron or fertiliser parcel, the superintendent wants to know what the cargo has done to the holds, and a gauging programme turns a visual impression into numbers. Other jobs come from sale and purchase activity and from ships preparing for a docking on another part of the Marmara. Scope follows what the discharge window allows and is agreed with the agent and the master.
list: Tank top and lower hold frame gauging on a Handysize bulk carrier after discharging boron products, with coating breakdown marked on the hold plan.
Hold and hopper plating readings on a Supramax bulk carrier following fertiliser raw material discharge, ahead of a grain loading.
Hatch coaming and hatch cover gauging on a general cargo ship after a deficiency was recorded at a previous Paris MoU port.
Ramp, car deck and ballast tank gauging on a ro-ro ship during a layover on the scheduled route.
Pre-purchase gauging on a second-hand Handysize bulk carrier at the bay anchorage, with the buyer's surveyor attending by launch.
Pre-docking gauging on an older coaster alongside, supplying a Marmara yard with a steel list before arrival.

logistics: The team flies into Istanbul and travels to Bandırma by road across the Osmangazi Bridge and through Bursa, or by sea connection from Istanbul where timetables suit. The ship's agent arranges port passes, launches to the bay anchorage and the terminal's permit and gas-free requirements, and receives crew lists, certificates and equipment details in advance. Indian passport holders need a Turkish visa, so we start the application when the call is nominated and keep the validity period wide enough to absorb a changed berth.

faqs.q: Can you gauge holds after a boron or fertiliser discharge?
faqs.a: Yes, once the cargo is out and the crew has swept and washed the holds to the point of safe entry. We concentrate on tank tops, lower frames, hopper plating and coamings, and record coating condition alongside the readings. The sequence is agreed with the chief officer to avoid delaying the next loading.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Bandırma?
faqs.a: Not for larger merchant ships. Docking and steel renewal normally happen at the Tuzla yards, in Yalova or at another Marmara yard. We report Bandırma readings by compartment so they can go straight to the yard to support the steel estimate and shorten planning once the ship is booked in.

faqs.q: Can ro-ro ships be gauged between voyages?
faqs.a: Yes, within the layover on their regular schedule. Ramps, car decks and ballast tanks are the usual targets, and access is arranged around loading so we are not in the way of the vehicle work. Windows can be short, so a prioritised plan is agreed with the master and agent beforehand.

faqs.q: Can a ship at the bay anchorage be gauged?
faqs.a: Yes, by launch booked through the agent. The bay is calmer than the open Marmara, so transfers are usually practical, but the ship may be called to the berth at short notice. We agree a priority list and take the most important deck, hatch and ballast tank readings first.
